meta.tagline: Free tiers for developers — verified, with the traps highlighted

tools.name: Vercel
tools.summary: Hobby plan: static + serverless hosting for personal projects.
traps: Commercial use is not allowed on Hobby
Hard caps: functions stop working when limits are hit

tools.name: Netlify
tools.summary: Free plan is now credit-based: 300 credits/month to spend on deploys, bandwidth and compute.
limits: ≈ 15 GB bandwidth (20 credits/GB) or ~20 production deploys (15 credits each)
traps: Sites STOP SERVING traffic when credits run out (until next cycle)
Frequent production deploys burn credits fast

tools.name: Cloudflare Workers + Pages
tools.summary: The most generous free hosting: unlimited static requests, serverless at the edge, KV/D1/R2 included.
limits: D1 (SQLite): 5 GB storage, 5M row reads / day
traps: 10 ms CPU limit rules out heavy compute per request
Daily (not monthly) quotas — a traffic spike can exhaust a day

tools.name: Render
tools.summary: Free web services + static sites; closest thing to the old Heroku free tier.
limits: No persistent disks, no SSH on free
traps: Services spin down after 15 min idle (~1 min cold start)
Free Postgres EXPIRES 30 days after creation — data deleted
Free Redis is in-memory only, data lost on restart

tools.name: Railway
tools.summary: One-time $5 trial credit (30 days), then a tiny $1/month free credit.
limits: $5 one-time trial credit, expires in 30 days
After trial: $1 free credit / mo (doesn't accumulate)
Trial: max 1 GB RAM, 5 services per project
traps: Trial volumes are DELETED 30 days after credits expire
$1/mo runs a real service for only a few days
Restricted outbound network unless verified via GitHub

tools.name: GitHub Pages
tools.summary: Free static hosting straight from a repo. Boring, reliable, hard to beat for docs and sites.
traps: Sites in free private repos must be public
Soft limits: heavy traffic can get your site throttled

tools.name: GitHub Actions
tools.summary: CI/CD built into GitHub. Unlimited for public repos; metered minutes for private ones.
traps: macOS runners burn minutes at 10x rate, Windows at 2x
Pricing shake-up announced Dec 2025: hosted runner prices cut, self-hosted runner fee proposed then postponed — watch this space

tools.name: Supabase
tools.summary: Postgres + auth + storage + realtime in one free package. Great to start, aggressive pausing.
traps: Projects PAUSE after 1 week of inactivity (manual restore)
No backups / PITR on free
Paused long enough — project can be removed

tools.name: Neon
tools.summary: Serverless Postgres with branching. One of the cleanest free DB tiers right now.
traps: Scale-to-zero after 5 min idle (can't be disabled) — first query after idle is slow
Compute suspends for the rest of the month if CU-hours run out

tools.name: Turso
tools.summary: Edge SQLite (libSQL). Big storage for a free tier, read-heavy friendly.
traps: SQLite semantics — not a drop-in Postgres/MySQL replacement
Write quota is 50x smaller than read quota

tools.name: MongoDB Atlas (M0)
tools.summary: Free shared MongoDB cluster. Small but stable — has existed for years without cuts.
traps: Clusters idle for 60+ days can be auto-paused
No backups on M0; some ops (e.g. $out) unsupported

tools.name: Upstash
tools.summary: Serverless Redis + queues + vector DB, priced per request. Free tier has been stable for years.
traps: Per-command pricing model: a chatty client library can eat the quota

tools.name: Firebase (Spark)
tools.summary: Google's app backend. Free Spark plan still strong for Firestore + Auth, but shrinking.
limits: Cloud Functions: requires Blaze (pay-as-you-go) plan since 2025
traps: Cloud Storage was REMOVED from the free Spark plan (Feb 2026)
Deep lock-in to proprietary Google APIs
Easy to silently graduate into a paid Blaze bill

tools.name: Clerk
tools.summary: Drop-in auth components. Free tier recently jumped to 50k monthly retained users.
traps: MRU counts users who RETURN 24h+ after signup — different metric than MAU
No MFA, passkeys or SMS auth on free
7-day fixed session lifetime

tools.name: Auth0
tools.summary: Enterprise-grade auth with a generous MAU cap. Feature gates, not user counts, push you to paid.
traps: Real ceiling is features: richer MFA, custom domains, enterprise SSO are paid
Paid tiers get expensive fast once you cross them

tools.name: Resend
tools.summary: Developer-first transactional email. The default free choice since SendGrid killed its free plan.
traps: The 100/day cap is what you hit first — bursts (launch day!) get throttled

tools.name: Sentry
tools.summary: Error tracking + performance. Free Developer plan covers a solo project comfortably.
traps: 1 seat only — no teammates on free
A crash-loop in production can blow the month's error quota in minutes (set rate limits!)

tools.name: Grafana Cloud
tools.summary: Managed metrics + logs + traces with a 'free forever' tier. No card required.
traps: 14-day retention — no long-term history
Careless Prometheus labels multiply active series fast

tools.name: Cloudinary
tools.summary: Image/video CDN with on-the-fly transforms. Credit-based free tier, stable for years.
limits: 25 monthly credits (1 credit = 1 GB storage OR 1 GB bandwidth OR 1k transformations)
Up to ~25 GB storage or bandwidth if used for one thing
traps: Credits are shared across storage, bandwidth AND transforms — they interact
Popular images with many transform variants eat credits quickly

tools.name: Cloudflare R2
tools.summary: S3-compatible object storage with ZERO egress fees — the killer feature.
limits: 1M class A + 10M class B operations / mo
traps: Requires a Cloudflare account with billing enabled to activate R2

tools.name: Oracle Cloud (Always Free)
tools.summary: Absurdly large 'Always Free' VMs: up to 4 ARM cores + 24 GB RAM. The catch is availability and reclaims.
limits: 4 OCPU ARM Ampere + 24 GB RAM (splittable into VMs)
traps: Card required at signup; ARM capacity often 'out of stock' in popular regions
Idle instances on free accounts can be RECLAIMED — keep some CPU activity
Account termination stories are common; keep backups elsewhere

graveyard.name: Heroku
graveyard.what: The original free PaaS: free dynos + free Postgres
graveyard.note: Killed all free plans citing abuse; pushed users to $5+/mo Eco dynos.

graveyard.name: Railway (unlimited free)
graveyard.what: The generous $5/mo recurring free credit era
graveyard.note: Now a one-time $5 trial for 30 days, then $1/mo. Trial volumes deleted 30 days after expiry.

graveyard.name: PlanetScale
graveyard.what: Free MySQL: 5 GB storage, 1B row reads/mo
graveyard.note: Free tier removed for existing users too; thousands forced to migrate. Now from $39/mo.

graveyard.name: Fly.io
graveyard.what: Free allowances: 3 shared VMs + 3 GB volumes
graveyard.note: Moved to pure pay-as-you-go for new accounts. No free tier.

graveyard.name: SendGrid
graveyard.note: Replaced by a 60-day trial. After that: pay or stop sending.

graveyard.name: Firebase Cloud Storage (Spark)
graveyard.what: Free 5 GB file storage on the Spark plan
graveyard.note: Cloud Storage now requires the paid Blaze plan; free tier keeps Firestore + Auth.
